problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(2,3,-1)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
$r=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$
worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨2,3,-1⟩.$ From the vectorial equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨3,2,-2⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨3,2,-2⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,2,-2⟩ & =⟨2,3,-1⟩\cdot ⟨3,2,-2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,2,-2⟩ & =14.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨3,2,-2⟩ & =14 \\ 3x+2y-2z & =14 \\ 3x+2y-2z-14 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
